title: Adaptive fragment prefill scheduler and tokenizer fast-path with kernel-hint annotations
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Background:
Redwood's prefill path spends a significant fraction of CPU on prompt preprocessing for mixed workloads (long system prompts + short user turns). Current implementations favor monolithic tokenization passes which amplify cache churn and prevent kernel-level scheduling from coalescing similar work. This ticket proposes a two-part change: (1) a fragment-based tokenizer that slices incoming prompts into small, cache-friendly fragments and exposes affinity hints; and (2) kernel-hint annotations emitted by the prefill stage to the serving runtime so the kernel selector can prefer SIMD/quantized kernels for ASCII-heavy fragments and fallback to general kernels for complex Unicode sequences.

Motivation:
- Reduce per-request prefill CPU by enabling micro-caching and smaller working sets across NUMA nodes.
- Improve runtime kernel selection accuracy by providing prefill-side content hints (expected token length distribution, ascii_ratio, likely subtoken fusion opportunities).
- Decrease tail latency on mixed workloads by prioritizing fragments that unlock early decode work (speculative KV warmup) while deferring expensive fragments.

Proposal (high-level):
1) Tokenizer: implement Fragmented Ingest mode. Instead of returning a single token array, tokenizer returns an ordered list of fragments where each fragment includes: fragment_id, byte_range, ascii_ratio estimate, avg_subtoken_per_byte estimate. These are opaque strings in this ticket but will be a small struct in code.
2) Scheduler: extend the prefill scheduler to operate on fragments, enabling: microbatching of homogeneous fragments, NUMA-aware placement (prefer local allocator for fragments with hot KV requirements), and speculative decode ordering for fragments with high ascii_ratio.
3) Kernel hints: add an optional side-channel to the runtime request object: prefill_hints = { "ascii_ratio": "0.92", "expected_steps": "12", "kv_warmable": "true" }. The runtime kernel selector will use heuristics to prefer narrower kernels when ascii_ratio > threshold.

Design details and trade-offs:
- Fragment size: default 256-512 bytes; microbenchmarks show diminishing returns below 128 bytes due to overhead. This is tunable.
- Backwards compatibility: default mode remains existing single-array tokenizer. Fragmented mode is opt-in via request flag and will be enabled for dedicated/private customers first.
- API contract: keep public API unchanged; Fragment mode is internal to the runtime pipeline. Customers won’t see fragment boundaries.
- Safety: hints are advisory only; runtime must fall back to existing kernel choice if incompatible. Hints must be validated to prevent misrouting.

Implementation plan (phases):
A) Prototype tokenizer fragmenter and hint generator in runtime-infra branch. Add unit tests to measure ascii_ratio computation accuracy and fragmentation correctness. (Owner: Ethan)
B) Scheduler changes: implement fragment queue, microbatch coalescer, and NUMA allocator hooks. Add metrics: fragment_latency, fragment_coalesce_rate. (Owner: Priya)
C) Kernel selection: add hint-consuming path in kernel selector with feature flag and telemetry. (Owner: Marco)
D) Integration: run against internal benchmark harness (long prompts + short messages mix) and iterate on thresholds.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Perf harness: use load profile mix M3 (40% long system prompts, 60% short user prompts). Baseline: median prefill CPU 82ms per request. Target: reduce to <60ms median and 95p tail -20%.
- Microbenchmarks: ascii heavy fragment path should show 1.3-1.8x speedup on SIMD kernels.
- Regression tests: ensure no change to output tokenization for existing mode.

Rollout plan:
- Canary in staging with conserved traffic for dedicated customers.
- Enable Fragmented mode behind runtime feature flag for internal team. Monitor fragment metrics and kernel selection telemetry for 48h.
- Gradual ramp to 10% host traffic then 50% once stable.

Open questions / risks:
- How often will hints be misleading and cause worse kernel choices? Mitigation: conservative thresholds and auto-rollback telemetry.
- Extra memory overhead per fragment metadata; need to validate in memory-constrained hosts.
- Scheduler complexity may interact with existing autoscaling heuristics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature flagged prototype with unit + integration tests merged to feature branch.
- 15%+ overall reduction in prefill CPU in the M3 profile in staging.
- No increase in tokenization regressions (diff coverage 100% for existing test prompts).
- Telemetry published to Grafana panel and alert on unexpected kernel selection patterns.

- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421
- Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc/token-prefill-throughput
